Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Improve hearing in left ear; understand and manage tinnitus
- Clinical Goal(s): Determine cause of unilateral hearing loss (rule out cerumen impaction or other pathology); provide education on tinnitus; plan appropriate follow-up
- Actions (Patient):
  • Attend face-to-face ear examination within 4–5 days  
  • Read tinnitus information leaflet provided via consultation notes  
  • Contact support team to schedule appointment; seek earlier review if symptoms worsen
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Arrange in-person otoscopic examination (admin team to book)  
  • Provide patient with tinnitus education link and support team phone number  
  • Document findings for continuity of care; consider onward ENT referral based on examination results

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of tinnitus, limited treatment options, need for otoscopic assessment
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased dizziness, sudden worsening of hearing, onset of pain or discharge
- Coping Strategies: Use background noise (TV/music) to mask tinnitus as patient already finds helpful
